readiness.mainReason: No blocking rule fired, the decision is clear and what remains would only tidy the deck.
readiness.highestRiskIssue: Two slides share a chart title on slides 11 and 12, which slows a skimming reader.
readiness.whatCouldChangeIt: Source notes for the figures were not supplied, and seeing them could change the evidence read.

dimensions.name: Recommendation specificity
dimensions.note: A named supplier and a date.

strengths.point: The recommendation is a single named action the client can act on.
strengths.quote: Client Z should switch to Supplier B.

findings.title: Slides 11 and 12 carry the same chart title, so a reader cannot tell what changed between them.
findings.principle: Slide titles carry the argument, not the label.
findings.diagnosis: Two consecutive slides are titled identically with no action title distinguishing them.
findings.why: A skimming reader treats the pair as a duplicate.
findings.reflect: What does each slide prove that the other does not?
findings.fix: Give each slide the action title that states its own point.

findings.title: The agenda names sections rather than the argument the deck is about to make.
findings.principle: An agenda can carry the storyline instead of the table of contents.
findings.diagnosis: The agenda lists six section labels with no through line.

evidence.quote: Context. Current spend. Supplier options. The saving. Rollout. Next steps.

findings.why: The reader waits until late in the deck to learn what it concludes.
findings.reflect: If the reader only read the agenda, what would they know?
findings.fix: Write the agenda as the argument in sequence.

findings.title: The depot count is stated in context and never used again in the analysis.
findings.principle: Context earns its place by returning later.
findings.diagnosis: Slide 3 gives the network size, and no later slide uses it to size anything.

evidence.quote: Client Z is a logistics co-operative serving 60 member depots across two regions.

findings.why: The reader cannot tell whether scale matters to the recommendation.
findings.reflect: Does the depot count change what you would recommend?
findings.fix: Either use the depot count in the rollout or drop it from the context.

learningNote.lesson: A tidy deck can still be missing the number its recommendation rests on.
learningNote.weakHabit: Reviewing the surface before the spine.
learningNote.exercise: Name the one figure the recommendation depends on, then look for its build.

notAssessed: Source notes were not supplied, so figure provenance was not assessed.
Slides 6 and 7 are image only in the extract.
